primary_reference: Campbell, Gilbert, Myers, The Science of Brass Instruments (2021), chapter 6

source_prescribed_approximation.scope: Book distinguishes prescribed-input propagation simulations from simulations including nonlinear feedback to the player. This implementation uses the former approximation, driven by the existing Adachi-Sato / linear-bore solver.

nonlinear_equation.normalization: q = p D(x)/D(0); coefficient beta/(rho*c^3)*D(0)/D(x), derived directly from Eq.6.34.

analytic_validation.test: Fubini solution, sigma=0.6, harmonics 1 through 6. Separate entropy-decay and refinement checks after shock formation at sigma=2.

losses.wall: Leading Keefe sqrt(f) attenuation and dispersion from chapter 4, matched to the existing model. Generalised Burgers wall-loss treatment discussed on pp.291-293.
losses.volume: Classical sound-diffusivity term. eta=1.846e-5 Pa s; thermal conductivity 0.0262 W/(m K) and Cp=1005 J/(kg K) are assumed representative values, not a fitted measurement of the instrument. Bulk viscosity and molecular relaxation omitted.

explicit_limitations: One-way propagation, prescribed incident wave; no nonlinear return-wave feedback to lips.
Flare-induced internal reflections and dispersion not recovered by the one-way variable-area equation, as discussed in the book p.295.
Mouthpiece itself remains in the existing linear acoustic subsystem; nonlinear propagation starts just after it.
Weakly nonlinear approximation; maximum source Mach number is reported in verification.json.
Finite-grid entropy dissipation participates in shock regularisation; microscopic shock thickness is not resolved.
Compact radiation approximation at 1 m, no nonlinear propagation outside the bell.
comparison: The matched linear reference sets beta=0 with exactly the same input, geometry, wall/volume losses, radiation and gain. It is a different propagation approximation from the original full TMM-radiation WAV.
